examples.label: night-train-chopper
originalLines: Quarter past midnight, the platform is vacant,
A timetable trembling, the ink almost faded.
The rail hums a warning through puddles and pavement,
I fold up the map but I can't fold the waiting.
Tickets in pockets, the clock doesn't listen,
Conductor says, "Board," with a spark in his vision.
A fast little rhythm of wheels in the distance—
Then silence. One foot on the step. One decision.

examples.label: sundial-courtroom
originalLines: The sundial sued the moon for overtime pay,
Said, "I work till dusk, then you steal my display."
The moon brought receipts from a cloudy July,
Said, "Your honor, that shadow was mostly the sky."
The clock in the gallery ticked with delight;
The jury of candles stayed up through the night.
They settled at dawn with a handshake and sigh—
The sun missed the hearing. No reason why.

examples.label: river-ferry
originalLines: My hands kept the ferry aligned with the shore,
Just one thin white line where the ropes scraped the floor.
A passenger asked why I never looked back;
I pointed ahead where the sunlight went black.
We crossed in a drizzle; the engine ran low,
A child held a paper boat steady below.
I finally turned when the harbor bell rang—
The shore hadn't moved, but the silence had changed.

examples.label: greenhouse-melody
originalLines: Under the glass where the winter winds go,
One little green stem is learning to grow.
Hold on, small light, hold on through the cold,
The night cannot measure the warmth you can hold.
I carry the water in jars from the hall,
Catch every bright drop before it can fall.
Hold on, small light, the morning is near,
Your leaves are the answer I needed to hear.

examples.label: street-violin-duel
originalLines: VIOLIN: I carry a storm in a whisper of string,
DRUMMER: I give it a road; hear the pavement ring.
VIOLIN: You rattle the windows, but can you be still?
DRUMMER: I can. One tap. Now follow the hill.
VIOLIN: I'll bend that last note till it circles your feet,
DRUMMER: I'll leave you a pocket right under the beat.
TOGETHER: No winner was needed; the crowd understood—
A challenge gets sharper when both players are good.

examples.label: lantern-maker
originalLines: The lantern maker hid a compass in the frame,
Wrote a crooked little arrow, never signed a name.
The apprentice held it up against the evening rain,
Saw a road through the market in the pattern of the grain.
At the bridge, a stranger asked him what the light was for;
He said, "A door I haven't found, or maybe just a shore."
Then the lantern caught the wind, and every wall turned gold—
The map was not a secret. It was courage being told.

examples.label: chess-club
originalLines: I walked into the chess club, quiet as a check,
They judged me by the pawns that I hadn't moved yet.
Old man tapped the timer like he knew the whole play,
I said, "A clock is not a compass; it can't choose my way."
Two bishops drew a hallway, his knight came round the bend,
I put my rook in danger just to change what he defended.
No crown on the table, no speech to impress—
I lost that first board and learned something from the mess.

examples.label: bus-stop
originalLines: The bus-stop roof was leaking through a rusted silver seam,
I watched the water sketch a crooked little stream.
A stranger held a book with the corners turned to gray,
Said, "Some pages look more honest once the ink has washed away."
We talked about the weather till the buses stopped arriving,
The streetlights blinked in pairs like the city was deciding.
I went home with no answers and a ticket in my coat,
But one kind conversation kept my tired feet afloat.

examples.label: library-elevator
originalLines: The lift says, "Floor of Doubt," and I'm holding down three,
A bookshelf wearing slippers asks what I'd like to be.
Next stop: Second Chances, where the mirrors are delayed;
They show the moves I almost made, the calls I almost made.
I press the button marked "Enough," it flickers into blue,
The elevator opens on a room I walked straight through.
No prophecy, no portal, just the library at ten—
I borrow one small paperback and ride the lift again.

examples.label: projector-blues
originalLines: Projector cough, projector cough, the pictures lost their place,
A cowboy took the spaceship and the alien won the race.
Projector cough, projector cough, I tried to slow the reel,
But the villain met a baker and forgot the way to steal.
The audience was laughing, so I let the stories roam,
A dragon bought a train ticket and finally went home.
The manager said, "Fix it," when the credits faded out—
I told him folks had paid to see what accidents were about.

examples.label: space-socks
originalLines: Somebody lost a sock in the orbital machine,
Now the oxygen is humming and the filters all are green.
The captain called a meeting, everybody brought a chart,
One engineer suggested we should launch a laundry cart.
The station AI whispered, "I have solved the mystery":
The missing sock was hanging by the emergency key.
We cheered and cut the power to the blinking red alarm,
Then somebody asked the question, "Where'd the other sock go, Marv?"

examples.label: old-mailbox
originalLines: The mailbox on the corner had no house behind its name,
Just a crooked little post where the lilacs still remained.
A letter came in winter with a stamp I'd never seen,
I kept it in my pocket till the first day turning green.
I found the old street register and traced the address down,
Delivered it to someone who had moved across the town.
She read it at the doorway and then asked me in for tea—
Not every lost thing needs a map to find where it should be.

examples.label: weather-radio
originalLines: Static on the rooftop, thunder in the wire,
Every little signal climbs a little higher.
Send me a frequency; send me a sign,
The clouds have their language, but I'm learning mine.
Night becomes a spectrum, blue beyond the glass,
Every warning changes when the hardest hours pass.
Send me a frequency; let the morning shine,
The clouds keep their language; I can still speak mine.

examples.label: ice-sculptor
originalLines: Chisel in a hurry, the thermometer climbs,
A gallery of winter in the heat of summertime.
The statue's little fingers start to soften at the tips,
I catch a falling crystal as the afternoon light slips.
The judges crowd the doorway; the fans begin to groan.
I carve a river through the ice and let the water flow.
They ask me why it's melting. I tell them, "That's the art."
The sculpture lasts a minute. The river leaves a mark.

examples.label: printer-office
originalLines: The printer left a notice in the corporate break-room:
"Effective now, I'm quitting all the paper and perfume!"
The stapler called a meeting, the scanner took the chair,
The copier made a hundred signs and posted them everywhere.
The manager demanded that the contracts all be signed,
The printer said, "I'm sorry, but I'm out of dotted lines."
They settled on a weekend and a better coffee rate—
Now every page says, "Paid vacation." That's a pretty good rebate.

examples.label: moon-garden
originalLines: The dome was full of hairline cracks; the heater lost its tune,
A gardener checked the seedlings in a greenhouse on the moon.
She patched it with a silver strip and shared the final cup
Of water with a stubborn root that wouldn't give it up.
The radio kept asking for a status and a plan;
She said, "The leaves are standing. Do the best you can."
At dawn a little flower opened brighter than the screen—
No speech about forever. Just a petal, small and green.

examples.label: coastal-lighthouse
originalLines: Across the black horizon there's a sail beyond the foam,
The lighthouse glass is broken and the keeper stands alone.
He holds a shard of silver where the moon can find the sea,
And turns it toward the vessel like a hand upon a key.
Go slowly through the water, go slowly through the night,
A single broken mirror may be strong enough for light.
When morning finds the harbor and the sailors step ashore,
He sets that shard beside the lamp and sweeps the wooden floor.

examples.label: flea-market-robot
originalLines: The robot held a pocket watch, the vendor named a price,
It searched a faded memory of a garden full of ice.
"I only have a button and a song I cannot play,"
The merchant looked at both of them and nodded anyway.
A child wound the watch and heard it tick against the rain,
The robot stood beside the stall, remembering a name.
No grand reunion followed, and the market closed at four,
But it came back on Saturdays to help them sweep the floor.

examples.label: theater-stagehand
originalLines: The curtain rope was tangled, all the painted forests fell,
The stagehand watched the scenery collapse like a shell.
She turned the broken branches into ladders for the cast,
Made the missing mountains from the shadows that they cast.
The actors crossed the stage and saw the audience lean in,
A second set of footsteps struck a rhythm from the wings.
The critic called it fearless; she just carried home the glue—
Sometimes the show keeps moving when you make the failure new.

examples.label: firefly-messenger
originalLines: The meadow spoke in intervals, not syllables or signs,
A thousand little lanterns drew their questions in the pines.
I counted until counting felt like missing what was there,
And put the notebook down to let the cool air find my hair.
The brightest one went dark, then flashed beside a stream,
As though it had been trying not to wake a deeper dream.
I walked back through the grasses, with a question I could keep:
How many kinds of silence are awake while we are asleep?

examples.label: clockwork-parade
originalLines: Tick—one bird opens paper wings.
Tock—one brass dog forgets its spring.
Tick—one street folds under the band.
Tock—a child lifts the conductor's hand.
Tick—the wheels keep time without a guide.
Tock—the crowd starts marching side by side.
Tick—the clock is wrong, but no one minds.
Tock—the parade has learned to keep its time.

examples.label: mountain-rescue
originalLines: Climbing through granite with sleet on the harness,
Radio cracking; the weather goes hardest.
Boots on a ledge where the gravel keeps sliding,
Marking the footholds, not guessing the timing.
One rope. Two knots. Check the line.
Three voices answering, right on time.
We pull through the darkness, the ridge turning blue—
No medals. Just four of us making it through.

examples.label: pocket-atlas
originalLines: My pocket atlas opens to a road that isn't there,
The ink has moved the crossings like somebody moved the air.
I ask the oldest taxi where the bridge went overnight;
He draws a line in pencil and says, "Try that one at light."
I follow every arrow till the river comes in view,
The streets are all unfamiliar but the morning still feels true.
I fold the map beside me; it's as useful as before—
A map can show the turning. It can't walk you through the door.

examples.label: kitchen-duet
originalLines: BAKER: The dough needs another hour; the crowd is at the gate.
RIVAL: You can rush the rising, but you cannot rush the taste.
BAKER: Your flour's on my counter, your sugar's in my bowl.
RIVAL: Then maybe both our recipes were never ours alone.
BAKER: Put the oven up to temperature; I'll shape a final round.
RIVAL: I'll clear a little table, let the hungry people crowd.
TOGETHER: The sun is on the window and the first loaf's finally done—
A rivalry tastes sweeter when the neighbors get some.
